name: Forge Auto International Limited
sector: Forged and machined automotive and industrial components
summary:
Forge Auto is a small, integrated forging and machining manufacturer, not yet an evidenced high-quality compounder. Qualification know-how and long operating experience are real; the decisive investment question is whether reported growth and profit convert into cash after the newly acquired machining subsidiary, intra-group flows and debt service are properly reconciled. At the dated ₹96.30 close the headline 8.53× reported earnings looks inexpensive, but cash-flow classification, loan conversion, refinancing and whole-lot liquidity materially weaken that inference.
The classification is research/watchlist only: a cyclical manufacturing/integration case with unresolved evidence, not a supported buy or a numerical ranking candidate. BQS, Growth Quality Score and IAS are NS. A lower quotation by itself would not repair the funding or information gaps. A comparable eliminated revenue/cash bridge, attributable reinvestment returns and verified current bank headroom could change the conclusion.

gates.name: Governance integrity
gates.reason: No demonstrated severe governance breach, but material connected-company lending/conversion and minority-owner safeguards need reconciliation.

gates.name: Information reliability
gates.reason: Reported statements are audited, but material CFO financing/noncash and acquisition-perimeter bridges are unresolved. This is an analytical hold, not an allegation that the opinion is qualified.

gates.name: Survival and funding
gates.reason: March audited debt is known; October sanctioned headroom/rollovers are not verified. Current funding cannot be assumed from the absence of reported default.

gates.name: Implementation
gates.reason: The stock trades but 1,200-share lots and low observed participation capacity make the ₹5 lakh reference difficult to exit. Live depth/spread is unverified.

GOV.reason: Operating history and clean opinions support a middle-band assessment; connected-company lending, subsequent acquisition/loan conversion and remuneration warrant active minority-owner scrutiny. No verified misappropriation, default or adverse auditor resignation is alleged.
GOV.what_changes_score: Acquisition independent valuation, cash/noncash reconciliation, current encumbrances and minority safeguards.
GOV.scale: 1–10; higher is stronger, except NS means unscored

MOAT.reason: Qualification, dies and process know-how create switching friction, but concentrated non-exclusive customers, steel pass-through exposure and absent evidence of superior through-cycle margins limit the advantage. Certifications alone do not establish pricing power.
MOAT.what_changes_score: Customer retention and share-of-wallet, rejected/requalified supplier costs, sustained relative unit margins.
MOAT.scale: 1–10; higher is stronger, except NS means unscored

REV.reason: The five-year reported CAGR is measurable at 15.60% and three-year at 8.58%, but neither establishes economic constant-scope growth after a material change in related-company flows. The external-parent cross-check is negative 7.22%. Under the framework obscured-demand rule, the scored basis cannot be established reliably; no arbitrary acquisition haircut or attractive-window choice.
REV.missing_evidence: Comparable eliminated group sales across FY25/FY26, acquisition-period revenue and a volume/price/mix bridge. Reported schedule candidates 7 and 4 are diagnostics only, not assigned scores.
REV.what_changes_score: Comparable eliminated group sales across FY25/FY26, acquisition-period revenue and a volume/price/mix bridge. Reported schedule candidates 7 and 4 are diagnostics only, not assigned scores.
REV.scale: 1–10; higher is stronger, except NS means unscored

DUR.reason: Auto, tractor, industrial and railway uses offer repeat replacement/OEM demand; application breadth is helpful, but customer concentration and cyclicality constrain visibility. Expansion capability is observable, not a multi-year booked revenue guarantee.
DUR.what_changes_score: Dated qualified programs, customer/product mix and funded demand visibility across the next capacity phase.
DUR.scale: 1–10; higher is stronger, except NS means unscored

CAP.reason: No meaningful attributable incremental return or unit/cohort economics is established. Core-capital proxies are disclosed but old-asset utilization, group sales, disposals and acquisition scope distort attribution. Current ROCE cannot fill this factor.
CAP.missing_evidence: Acquisition-date economic capital including assumed obligations, commissioning dates and attributable project NOPAT/cash economics.
CAP.what_changes_score: Acquisition-date economic capital including assumed obligations, commissioning dates and attributable project NOPAT/cash economics.
CAP.scale: 1–10; higher is stronger, except NS means unscored

CASH.reason: Financing inflows sit inside reported CFO; noncash loan conversion and first-year consolidation remain unreconciled. Removing only borrowing is necessary but insufficient. Historical weak after-interest cash conversion is shown without inventing a normalized FY26 cash number.
CASH.missing_evidence: Cash/noncash and acquisition-date opening balance reconciliation, bank cash statements, working-capital ageing and supplier-credit movements.
CASH.what_changes_score: Cash/noncash and acquisition-date opening balance reconciliation, bank cash statements, working-capital ageing and supplier-credit movements.
CASH.scale: 1–10; higher is stronger, except NS means unscored

BAL.reason: Audited net debt/operating EBITDA is 2.73× with 3.12× EBIT interest cover, very little clearly unrestricted cash and material demand facilities. The asset base and no reported default prevent an automatic failure, but resilience depends on renewal.
BAL.what_changes_score: Current sanctioned limits, drawing power, maturity and covenant headroom; verified free cash and funding commitments.
BAL.scale: 1–10; higher is stronger, except NS means unscored

EXEC.reason: IPO use and installed machinery milestones are documented, and acquisition completed. Returns from integration and new capacity are not proven; no penalty is applied simply for absence of numerical guidance.
EXEC.what_changes_score: Delivered group throughput, efficiency and cash returns from acquired/commissioned assets, not just installed capacity.
EXEC.scale: 1–10; higher is stronger, except NS means unscored

EARN.reason: Standalone PAT rose 13.51% but diluted EPS slipped from ₹10.01 to ₹9.91; reported consolidated EPS₹11.29 has no comparable group prior-year base. Other income is stripped from operating earnings and a 25% analytical tax is explicit.
EARN.what_changes_score: Comparable eliminated profit and per-share bridge, normalized margins and recurring earnings versus incentive/interest income.
EARN.scale: 1–10; higher is stronger, except NS means unscored

R.reason: A material current funding package is not verified and the ordinary base case runs out of cash. A hypothetical equity rescue is not a supported base-case return. No R is computed from the rescue or optimistic bull case.

R.what_changes_score: Verified funding and acquisition/cash reconciliations sufficient to produce a defensible funded ordinary shareholder return.
R.scale: 1–10; higher is stronger, except NS means unscored

D.reason: Credible stress combines weaker orders/margins, slower working capital and debt service. It requires ₹39.95 cr hypothetical rescue; new equity at half the entry quote leaves original holders with about 56.8% of shares and a negative conditional five-year return.
D.what_changes_score: Lower leverage, verifiable collections/cash reserves, committed refinancing and downside asset recovery support.
D.scale: 1–10; higher is stronger, except NS means unscored

P.reason: Headline multiples are undemanding, but modest growth cannot meet the model cash schedule without funding. The algebraic 15% hurdle solution still needs ₹7.98 cr capital; a base rescue at half-price earns only 13.91%. Several financing/working-capital assumptions must hold together.
P.what_changes_score: Supported conservative funded cases meeting the hurdle without relying on margin expansion, dilution assumptions or rerating.
P.scale: 1–10; higher is stronger, except NS means unscored

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Exact issuer: Forge Auto International Limited; NSE Emerge FORGEAUTO; ISIN INE0YKW01013; CIN U25910PB2023PLC058272. The predecessor Auto International partnership began in 2001; company conversion was 25 April 2023 and public-company conversion 1 June 2024. Use the accounting-policy/prospectus chronology rather than a stray 2025 conversion reference in the FY26 board report. NSE listing was 4 October 2024, not the 1 October date in one timeline graphic.
Information cutoff 20 October 2026. Market observation: official 19 October 2026 close ₹96.30; 2,400 shares, two trades. Current issued shares 10.92 million give ₹105.1596 cr equity value. Latest audited accounts end 31 March 2026; AS accounting rather than IndAS. Historical full economic/predecessor and corporate partial-year scopes are not interchanged. First-year consolidated FY26 is used only as a qualified forecast scale. No FY27 interim has been verified at cutoff.
Horizon: 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031; 15% nominal INR equity hurdle before personal tax, with 12%/18% sensitivities. Liquidity reference ₹5 lakh is a convention, not personalized sizing. G1 Conditional, G2 Hold, G3 Hold, G4 Conditional. Confidence is high on exact identity, filed balances and market prints; medium on business/governance interpretation; low on organic growth, cash normalization, incremental returns and current funding. G3 Hold alone does not remove a company from quality comparison; here missing quality factors and G2 independently prevent ranking.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Primitive factors: GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV NS, DUR 5, CAP NS, CASH NS, BAL 4, EXEC 5, EARN 4, R NS, D 3, P 4, L 1. Each factor has its own evidence, confidence and change condition in the canonical factor audit. No missing factor is assigned a neutral 5.
BQS uses 20% GOV + 20% MOAT + 12% REV + 10% DUR + 12% CAP + 10% CASH + 8% BAL + 8% EXEC. Known contribution 3.02, coverage 66%; completion bounds 3.36–6.42. Growth Quality uses 40% REV + 20% DUR + 15% EARN + 15% CAP + 10% CASH: known contribution 1.60, coverage 35%, bounds 2.25–8.10. IAS uses 25% final BQS + 35% R + 20% D + 10% P + 10% L: known contribution 1.10, coverage 40%, bounds 1.70–7.10. All three final scores remain NS, not renormalized partial averages. Display bounds are 3.4–6.4, 2.3–8.1 and 1.7–7.1 using Decimal half-up rounding; bounds are not estimated ratings.
No numerical override is applied: GOV is above 3 and no gate is Fail; missing CAP/CASH are not interpreted as weak scores that activate a Growth Quality cap. Full exact weights, weighted contributions, coverage and bounds are embedded. The price does not change a quality factor, and the optimistic scenario does not create an R score.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The Ludhiana business makes closed-die hot-forged and machined parts in carbon/alloy steel, generally 1–20 kg, with aluminium forgings around 0.5–6 kg. Applications include passenger/commercial vehicles, tractors, agricultural machinery, railway and industrial equipment. The manufacturing chain includes dies, forging/pressing, heat treatment, finishing and machining. OEM/tier qualification and reliable dimensional quality matter; certifications support access but do not alone prove a moat.
Revenue is recognized on dispatch under the stated risk/reward policy; payment arrives later, while steel, work in process and finished goods tie up cash. FY26 consolidated inventories ₹80.3639 cr and receivables ₹37.0348 cr illustrate the capital intensity. Exports by the parent were ₹5.6047 cr, roughly 2.48% of standalone sales, versus ₹5.6592 cr the prior year. No current end-market revenue split or market share with a reliable denominator is verified.
Forge Mach Auto became a wholly owned subsidiary on 27 August 2025 for ₹2.401 cr purchase consideration. Parent equity investment reached ₹19.751 cr after a ₹17.35 cr loan conversion. On 6 October 2026 that subsidiary took 26% of KBM Renewables for ₹0.026 cr to support captive power. KBM had not commenced operations; neither future savings nor electricity revenue is added to the thesis.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The plausible advantage is qualification and process reliability: customer-specific dies, machining tolerances and rejection avoidance can make switching costly. The evidence is a long operating history, installed forging/machining capabilities and certifications. Durability is only moderate because capable suppliers can build equipment and qualify over time; current retention, sole-source status, rejection rates and price premium are not quantified. Entrant qualification duration and investment are ND, so no unsupported barrier estimate is assigned.
Failure mechanisms are clear: customer re-sourcing, raw-material pass-through lag, a product program ending, defects, or capacity installed before demand. FY24 top-ten customers represented 85.16% of sales and top-ten suppliers 78.95% of purchases. Orders were non-exclusive and did not guarantee continuing volume. Diverse applications should not be confused with diversified customers.
The prospectus names Balu Forge, MM Forgings, Happy Forgings and Samrat Forgings as operating references. Larger/heavier or more integrated forging mixes are not valuation twins. Their historical reported margins cannot be imported as a current peer multiple. Current peer quote/accounting/lease normalization is not established here, so the 5×/7×/9× terminal EV/EBITDA grid is a declared scenario convention rather than a peer-derived fair-value claim. MOAT 4 reflects modest switching friction without proof of sustained superior economics.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Reported economic/predecessor-to-standalone revenue in ₹cr: FY21 109.5199; FY22 132.8785; FY23 176.6485; FY24 180.1172; FY25 209.8943; FY26 226.1328. Absolute additions were 23.3586, 43.7700, 3.4687, 29.7771 and 16.2385. Five-year reported CAGR is 15.60%, four-year 14.22%, three-year 8.58%, and latest standalone growth 7.74%; 10-year history is unavailable. FY21 is a pandemic-period predecessor account, while FY24 full-year restated revenue must not be replaced with the ₹169.4188 cr corporate 25 April 2023–31 March 2024 partial period.
The important economic cross-check runs in the opposite direction: parent sales to FMAPL increased from ₹20.5695 cr to ₹50.4756 cr. Parent revenue excluding those disclosed sales fell from ₹189.3248 cr to ₹175.6572 cr, down 7.22%. This does not mean group external demand fell 7.22%: subsidiary external sales and acquisition-period eliminations are not fully bridged. Equally, comparing consolidated ₹270.1889 cr with prior standalone ₹209.8943 cr is not organic growth.
H1 standalone revenue rose from ₹106.1345 cr to ₹107.4399 cr, 1.23%; derived H2 rose from ₹103.7598 cr to ₹118.6929 cr, 14.39%. These periods still contain changing related-company flows. Volume, price, mix, currency and acquisition effects are ND separately. REV remains NS because the constant-scope economic growth basis is unresolved, not because small scale is penalized or the weakest window was chosen.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
A credible scaling route would combine more qualified customer programs with better utilization of existing forging and machining assets. FY24 parent forging utilization was 76.40% and machining 86.08%; these are dated historical observations, not available FY26 group spare capacity. New presses, ring rolling and FMAPL add capability, but verified present throughput, price per unit, commissioned capacity economics and customer-backed loading are missing. Captive power is an option to reduce costs, not a quantified return source.
The capital-efficiency appendix computes core invested-capital proxies from operating PPE/CWIP plus inventory and receivables less payables, and compares three-/four-year NOPAT changes. These are not attributable incremental ROIC: the scope excludes other operating balances, related sales changed, old assets may have improved utilization, disposals/depreciation matter, and acquisition capital is not reconciled. A 12–18% nominal-INR capital-cost sensitivity is shown, not asserted as observed WACC. No reliable five-year capital bridge or unit/cohort economics is available. CAP remains NS rather than substituting current ROCE.
Growth consumes funds. The illustrative 8% base keeps core working capital intensity at the audited 28.64% of sales, uses 3% cash capex, 1.7% depreciation, 10.2% EBITDA margin and 10% debt cost. Even assuming bank/related debt renewal, it requires ₹12.4257 cr of additional capital over five years under the stated amortization schedule. GQS is NS: growth, attributable reinvestment economics and sustainable cash conversion must be established together.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Rajan Mittal and Parmod Gupta lead an experienced promoter-controlled manufacturer. March 2026 promoter ownership was 73.63%; the residual 26.37% is a mechanical non-promoter share, not verified readily tradable free float. Current encumbrance details beyond the NSE indicators require confirmation. Unmodified audit opinions and CARO no-default reporting are positive but do not earn a high governance score by themselves.
Capital-allocation milestones: the 2024 IPO gross ₹31.104 cr was reported fully applied by May 2026 to ₹19 cr working capital, ₹5 cr loan repayment, ₹4.2634 cr general purposes and ₹2.8406 cr issue expenses. This is completed use, not unspent financing. The 27 August 2025 machining acquisition completed at ₹2.401 cr; subsequent ₹17.35 cr loan conversion changes the form of support rather than creating operating cash. Acquisition valuation, assumed external obligations and integration returns remain to be reconciled. The 6 October 2026 KBM commitment is ₹0.026 cr initially, but total project funding is ND.
Consolidated director remuneration ₹1.7063 cr equals 13.84% of PAT. Five relatives' salaries total ₹0.48 cr; combined 17.73% of PAT is material enough to monitor, not proof of abuse. Related-party sales, loans, job work and capital transfers are described rather than hidden in a generic governance label.
Promises versus delivery: machinery installation and IPO deployment are observable completed milestones; economic return targets and new program volume guidance are not verified. Acquisition is completed; profitable cash integration is still unproven. KBM incorporation is completed; power commissioning and savings are pending. No penalty is imposed for absence of promotional guidance. GOV 5 and EXEC 5 balance demonstrated operations with these open tests.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The prospectus KPI EBITDA of ₹7.1842/₹11.2855/₹13.7177 cr for FY22/FY23/FY24 differs from the consistently computed PBT  +  interest  +  depreciation − all other income bridge of ₹7.2167/₹11.3888/₹14.5141 cr. The definition difference is unresolved and the latter is used transparently, not silently mixed with peer KPIs. The canonical financial history retains the original lakh inputs and calculated ₹crore rows, including revenue, value-added proxy, EBITDA, EBIT, PAT, normalized PAT, current-sharebase EPS, CFO, interest, capex, FCF diagnostics, inventory, receivables, payables and core capital. Value added equals revenue minus materials and inventory changes before other manufacturing costs; it is not gross profit. Gross profit is ND because manufacturing expenses are mixed in other expenses. Normalized PAT excludes all other income and applies an analytical 25% tax, not a claim about sustainable statutory taxation.
FY24 full-year/FY25/FY26 standalone revenue was ₹180.1172/₹209.8943/₹226.1328 cr. Reported PAT₹6.6888/₹9.5293/₹10.8171 cr. FY26 standalone EPS₹9.91 was below ₹10.01 in FY25 despite 13.51% PAT growth because historical weighted shares differ. Consolidated ₹12.333 cr PAT and ₹11.29 EPS lack a comparable prior group year. Consolidated other income ₹1.7046 cr includes incentives, interest and rent; strict operating EBITDA is ₹27.4763 cr and EBIT₹22.8086 cr.
Reported CFO must not be read as organic cash: FY25 standalone CFO−₹7.1664 cr includes ₹1.0963 cr borrowing inflow; FY26 standalone ₹21.5780 cr includes ₹6.7005 cr; FY26 consolidated ₹24.2567 cr includes ₹18.5995 cr. Removing those items gives−₹8.2627 cr, ₹14.8775 cr and ₹5.6572 cr respectively, still before cash interest paid in financing and unresolved loan-conversion/acquisition adjustments. The ₹17.35 cr conversion is explicit in AR p.133. The consolidated cash-flow opening cash ₹2.0559 cr includes the subsidiary's prior-year ₹0.0395 cr despite acquisition in August; acquisition-related capital and borrowing movements require a dated elimination bridge. These are reconciliation flags, not accusations of fabricated accounts.
FY25 cash-flow comparatives were regrouped between investing and financing by ₹3.2904 cr of long-term advances; net cash was unchanged. FY24 prospectus restatement places short-term debt in financing, whereas later reports place changes inside operating cash flow. Consistent comparisons must undo that difference. Historical after-interest FCF is materially weaker than headline CFO/PAT suggests.
Inventory and receivable balances are examined in their own days versus sales, not compared as percentage growth against days. Parent inventory/revenue days climbed from 72.02 in FY24 to 95.81 in FY25 and 99.88 in FY26; receivable days moved 48.24, 37.08, 53.70. Current group inventory is ₹80.3639 cr, including ₹48.9680 cr finished goods, and stock ageing is ND. Parent ₹0.6893 cr doubtful debt was written off in FY26; low remaining over-six-month receivables do not prove every current balance is cash-like. Debt including finance leases ₹75.0265 cr, tiny free cash, a ₹2.0883 cr pledged SIDBI deposit and demand facilities make current funding headroom central. CASH is NS pending reconciliation.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹96.30 and 10.92 million shares, market cap is ₹105.1596 cr. Add ₹75.0265 cr interest-bearing debt including finance leases and deduct only ₹0.0534 cr clearly unrestricted cash to get ₹180.1327 cr EV. Reported consolidated P/E8.53×, EV/strict operating EBITDA 6.56×, P/B 1.51× and analytical normalized P/E9.05× are descriptors using March accounts, not an October funding confirmation. The ₹0.3307 cr deposits inside reported cash and ₹1.9391 cr other investments are not automatically treated as free cash; the separately pledged ₹2.0883 cr deposit is excluded. No NCI is reported at March; the later 26% associate does not create parent minority equity in the wholly owned subsidiary.
Five-year forecasts have every annual revenue, margin, EBIT, interest, tax, working-capital, capex, principal, cash, share-count and funding row embedded. Bear assumes an initial 15% revenue fall,7% margin recovering to 9%,35% core working capital and 12% debt cost; base assumes 8% growth, 10.2% margin and 7× exit EBITDA; bull assumes 15% growth,12–13% margin, working-capital compression to 25% and 9× exit. These are scenarios, not management guidance. Finance leases remain in debt and amortization; no dividend is also retained as terminal cash. Opening debt is not deducted twice.
Ordinary bear/base funding fails, with peak deficits ₹39.9481 cr/₹12.4257 cr; their terminal equity price and shareholder IRR are null. A separate hypothetical 50%-of-entry-price rescue issues new shares at ₹48.15: base terminal shares 1.3501 cr and conditional return 13.91%, below the 15% hurdle; bear shares 1.9217 cr and return−15.50%. These rescue terms are not committed financing. Bull is internally funded under conditional rollover/operating assumptions and yields 42.87%, but margin, cash release and rerating are jointly optimistic and cannot determine R.
Reverse algebra at 7× says the 15% hurdle needs 5.45% sales growth, but that very path has a ₹7.9757 cr funding hole, so it is not an investable low-expectations claim. Hurdle 12%/18% changes the algebraic growth requirement to 2.56%/8.35%, also unfunded. Growth versus terminal-multiple, interest/recall, collection-delay, rescue-price and 1%/3%/5% execution-cost sensitivities are included. No probability-weighted IRR, supported base entry price or unconditional fair-value range is asserted.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
Permanent-loss risk is High. The connected failure chain is lower customer orders and margins, slow collection or unsaleable finished goods, supplier-credit pressure, capex/service obligations and reduced bank drawing power. A lower quote is not the same as this economic impairment: forced recapitalization can transfer recovery value to new shareholders even if factories remain viable.
The bear model writes down 15% of opening inventory and 10% of receivables, a ₹15.7581 cr noncash capital impairment. It reduces opening recoverable working capital once; restoring the modeled operating stock then absorbs cash through the working-capital bridge. The loss is not also subtracted as a second cash expense. Five-year operating cash and term principal produce a ₹39.9481 cr peak capital gap before rescue. At the hypothetical ₹48.15 issue price, new equity increases shares to 1.9217 cr, original owners retain 56.83%, and conditional annualized return is−15.50%. Ordinary unsupported recovery remains null.
Additional stresses recall 20% or 100% of ₹38.3945 cr bank demand debt, increase interest to 12%, or add 15/30 days to collections. Each is linked to annual cash needs in the model rather than merely reducing a valuation multiple. Assets may have recovery value, but liquidation discounts, enforceable collateral priority and facility-specific recoveries are unverified; no book-value floor is claimed. No report of historical default is converted into a guarantee of future refinancing.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
Five times the ₹96.30 entry means ₹481.50 per share in 2031; ten times means ₹963.00, equivalent to 37.97% and 58.49% annualized shareholder returns before personal tax and costs. At the declared 7× terminal operating EBITDA and base 10.2% margin, the undiluted algebra requires 27.79% five-year revenue growth for 5×, ending near ₹920.78 cr sales; 10× requires 47.80%, ending near ₹1, 905.38 cr. Those are about 3.41×/7.05× the filed consolidated scale.
The critical qualification is funding: these algebraic paths require approximately ₹88.79 cr/₹265.99 cr additional capital under the same working-capital, capex and debt-service rules. They are therefore not ordinary shareholder outcomes and cannot be reported as feasible returns. New equity would change the per-share targets; more borrowing would change interest, risk and terminal claims. The separate rescue logic illustrates that trade-off rather than hiding it.
Historical parent sales growth, dated capacity utilization and current customer concentration do not establish accessible demand for those scales. Current group installed/commissioned capacity, unit prices, new-customer commitments, project capital and incremental returns are not verified sufficiently to translate these numbers into a physical production plan. The optimistic bull can exceed 5× only with materially better margins, working capital and a 9× exit multiple together. Neither 5× nor 10× is an evidenced central thesis.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Before quality or investment ranking: obtain a like-for-like FY25/FY26 group revenue bridge, monthly acquisition-period sales and inter-company eliminations; reconcile ₹17.35 cr noncash conversion and every financing line currently inside CFO; reconcile opening acquired balances, cash and consideration. Then rebuild normalized after-interest cash generation and per-share economics. These are concrete information requirements, not reasons to fill missing scores with 5.
Before an investability decision: verify October/current bank sanctions, drawing power, renewal/maturity schedules, covenant compliance, true free cash and committed funding for capex and KBM. Map acquisition economic capital and commissioned assets to attributable profit/cash. Obtain customer concentration, order terms, stock ageing and subsequent cash collections. Check whether standalone external sales recover rather than relying on the headline group increase.
Operating monitoring should track inventory/revenue days, receivable days and bad debt, supplier-credit ageing, normalized margins excluding incentives, debt service and diluted share count. Falsifiers include persistent external-parent contraction without group demand evidence, unexplained cash/noncash differences, adverse audit/scope changes, renewal shortfall or a recapitalization below the quoted price.
Liquidity detail: the 20-session mean/median traded values were ₹357,624/₹240,270 with two zero-trade sessions; the 60-session mean/median were ₹749,026/₹475,920 with eight. Continuous ₹5 lakh liquidation at 2%/5%/10% participation is 52.53/21.01/10.51 sessions on the conservative 60-day denominator, versus 104.05/41.62/20.81 on 20 days. These fractional-share capacity figures are not directly executable in a 1,200-share SME lot. Four lots cost ₹462,240 and five ₹577, 800. Strict 5% participation requires at least 24,000 shares of daily volume to place one lot. Only three lots of aggregate capacity appeared across two of 60 sessions, insufficient for either reference holding; repeat-window extrapolation is 80/100 sessions, not a fill promise. At 2% the analogous extrapolation is 240/300 sessions; at 10% it is 15/18.75 sessions. The 20-day 5% lot denominator is zero, so no finite estimate exists. All observed lot fields were 1, 200.
For implementation, recheck current eligible series, lot, surveillance, traded values and actual two-sided depth immediately before any order. Use a whole-lot reference matched to the intended holding; the historical model is not an exit promise. The next half-year filing and acquisition/funding clarifications are natural review events; no monitoring automation or external outreach is claimed to have been scheduled.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Classification: cyclical forging/machining integration candidate, evidence hold, high permanent-loss risk and poor reference-position liquidity. Not established as a high-quality compounder and not rejected solely because it is small or because G3 is Hold. GQS means Growth Quality, distinct from business quality and price-sensitive investment attractiveness.
BQS NS and GQS NS arise from missing REV/CAP/CASH evidence; IAS NS also lacks a defensible R and underlying BQS. Current quoted multiples cannot substitute for those facts. D 3/P 4/L 1 describe the modeled downside, assumption dependence and execution difficulty, not a personalized instruction to transact. This security remains outside numerical quality, growth-quality and investment ranking until the necessary evidence is scoreable.
The useful next step is reconciliation, not a price target. If audited/eliminated organic growth, cash realization and attributable returns become reliable, quality can be compared even while a separate funding gate remains Hold. A purchase case would additionally require a supported funded base path, acceptable downside and feasible execution for the actual position. No transaction has been performed.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary evidence is the exchange-hosted FY26/FY25 annual reports, final IPO prospectus, issuer-hosted audited predecessor and subsidiary accounts, filed interim/year-end results, the 6 October KBM disclosure, and dated NSE market/security/regulatory files. Every material claim has a source ID and locator; every daily liquidity input has its original URL/hash. The analysis uses only information published by 20 October 2026 despite retrieval on 21 October. Secondary discovery pages were not used to fill numerical evidence gaps.
Original PDFs and tax-audit files are retained locally for verification, but omitted from Library backup because they may contain unnecessary individual tax or national identifiers. The full private research backup preserves the financial facts, source URLs/hashes, all model rows, safe market extracts, scripts and QA, not unredacted personal identifiers. No internal framework or helper implementation is packaged for the reader.
Material assumptions: March balances carried unchanged to the dated quote; first consolidated revenue used as a qualified starting scale; constant other operating net balances; hypothetical loan amortization after year 1; conditional renewal of bank/related debt; no undrawn financing invented; no dividends; 25% cash tax without loss tax credits; no proceeds from restricted deposits or nonoperating investments; ₹0.026 cr KBM equity counted once. Scenario probabilities are not assigned.
Open questions remain explicit: acquisition-period consolidation and financing cash classification, organic external demand, loan-conversion reconciliation, current limits and encumbrances, stock ageing and project-specific returns, peer-normalized current valuation and live order-book spread. Minor filing chronology and rounding inconsistencies are retained as qualifications rather than silently overwritten. A source/model QA report accompanies the canonical data; structural QA does not certify undisclosed facts.

evidence.claim: Legal issuer is Forge Auto International Limited, CIN U25910PB2023PLC058272, FORGEAUTO, ISIN INE0YKW01013. Issued equity 10,920,000 shares; current regular lot 1,200 shares.
evidence.locator: AR26 pp.38–39,81 and 19 October security-master eligible SM row

evidence.claim: Reported full-year standalone/predecessor revenue FY21–26 is ₹109.5199 cr, ₹132.8785 cr, ₹176.6485 cr, ₹180.1172 cr, ₹209.8943 cr and ₹226.1328 cr. Five-year reported CAGR 15.60%; three-year 8.58%.
evidence.locator: FY21 audited trading account PDF p.26; prospectus printed pp.134–136; AR26 pp.110–112
evidence.qualification: The FY21 pandemic base and later related-company sales prevent treating this as verified organic growth.

evidence.claim: Sales by parent to Forge Mach Auto rose from ₹20.5695 cr in FY25 to ₹50.4756 cr in FY26. Parent sales excluding these fell 7.22%, from ₹189.3248 cr to ₹175.6572 cr.
evidence.locator: AR26 p.133; AR25 printed p.90/PDF p.91
evidence.qualification: This is an external-parent cross-check, not consolidated organic growth.

evidence.claim: Reported FY26 consolidated CFO ₹24.2567 cr contains ₹18.5995 cr of short-term-borrowing inflow in the operating section. Removing only that classified financing item gives ₹5.6572 cr, before acquisition/noncash reconciliation and cash interest.
evidence.qualification: Not presented as fully normalized CFO; interest is paid in financing in the filed cash-flow statement.

evidence.claim: ₹17.35 cr of loans to Forge Mach Auto was converted into equity; parent subsidiary investment ended at ₹19.751 cr. Loan conversion is noncash, not recurring operating cash.
evidence.locator: AR26 p.133 related-party table and p.125 investments
evidence.qualification: Allocation of noncash conversion across reported cash-flow captions is not fully reconciled.

evidence.claim: FY26 consolidated debt is ₹72.0497 cr plus ₹2.9768 cr finance leases. Bank demand borrowings are ₹38.3945 cr; unrestricted current accounts and cash total only ₹0.0534 cr under the conservative cash definition.
evidence.locator: AR26 pp.70,82–87; debt and cash notes
evidence.qualification: Fixed deposits are excluded unless unrestricted status is demonstrated; available October drawing power is not verified.

evidence.claim: FY26 consolidated revenue ₹270.1889 cr, PAT ₹12.3330 cr and operating EBITDA excluding all other income ₹27.4763 cr; EBIT interest coverage 3.12×.
evidence.qualification: First consolidation year; not a comparable organic growth series or independently verified current run-rate.

evidence.claim: FY24 top-ten customers supplied 85.16% of revenue; top-ten suppliers 78.95% of purchases. Customer purchase orders were non-exclusive and lacked committed continuing purchase volumes.
evidence.qualification: Current customer mix and concentration not disclosed at an equally detailed verified level.

evidence.claim: FY24 parent forging output 15, 279.59 MT of 20,000 MT capacity; machining output 2,152,123 pieces of 2,500,000 capacity. New presses/ring-rolling and subsidiary machining expand capability, but no attributable new-project economics is established.
evidence.locator: Prospectus business capacity table; AR25 business timeline; AR26 pp.6–12,73
evidence.qualification: Installed capacity is not demand, funded expansion or a verified incremental-return claim.

evidence.claim: The ₹31.104 cr IPO gross proceeds were reported fully used: ₹19 cr working capital, ₹5 cr debt repayment, ₹4.2634 cr general purposes and ₹2.8406 cr issue expenses.
evidence.locator: AR26 pp.39–40; May2026 IPO utilization certificate
evidence.qualification: Do not add IPO cash again to the March 2026 balance sheet.

evidence.claim: Auditors issued unmodified opinions; consolidation relies on the subsidiary auditor and highlights acquisition. CARO reported no loan default or wilful-default classification.
evidence.locator: AR26 consolidated auditor report pp.61–69 and standalone pp.98–109
evidence.qualification: Clean opinions do not resolve the analytical cash-flow/perimeter questions; no fraud or default conclusion is inferred.

evidence.claim: Promoter ownership was 73.63% at March 2026. Consolidated director remuneration was ₹1.7063 cr; disclosed salaries to five named relatives total ₹0.48 cr.
evidence.locator: AR26 p.81 shareholding and pp.92–94 remuneration/RPTs
evidence.qualification: Together these are about 17.73% of consolidated PAT; not all related-party flows are remuneration.

evidence.claim: 6 October 2026: wholly owned FMAPL subscribed ₹0.026 cr for 26% of KBM Renewables, a not-yet-operating captive-power associate. Additional project spending, capacity and funding are unverified.
evidence.qualification: No estimated power savings or renewable-energy revenue is credited.

evidence.claim: 19 October 2026 official close ₹96.30 on 2,400 shares and two trades. Sixty sessions contain eight zero-trade dates; conservative median turnover ₹475, 920. Five-percent continuous capacity implies 21.01 days for ₹5 lakh.
evidence.locator: 60 matched bhavcopy extracts and dated 19 October row
evidence.qualification: Zero activity is included only where the complete market archive is valid; no missing data silently filled.

evidence.claim: The 1,200-share lot is worth ₹115, 560. Strict 5% whole-lot participation allowed just three lots in two of 60 sessions; four/five lots were not completed within the observed window.
evidence.locator: Floor(volume × participation / 1200) over every valid session
evidence.qualification: Repeat-window estimate 80/100 sessions is an extrapolation, not a fill guarantee. A ₹5 lakh reference is not personal sizing advice.

evidence.claim: NSE current regulatory row is active SM; GSM/ASM/ESM are not applicable, while fewer than 100 unique traders in the preceding 30 days and irregular SME trading flags are triggered.
evidence.locator: 19 October REG1 FORGEAUTO row and NSE legend
evidence.qualification: No live spread, order-book depth or circuit-lock history is available; no inference of unrestricted execution.

evidence.claim: Parent half-year sales grew 1.23% in H1 FY26 and 14.39% in H2 FY26, but the period split does not isolate the changing related-company sales.
evidence.locator: H1 filing PDF p.2; H2 computed as full year less H1
evidence.qualification: No FY27 half-year results were verified by the 20 October cutoff; TTM is FY26 only.

evidence.claim: The funded-path model gives a ₹12.4257 cr base cumulative funding deficit and ₹39.9481 cr stress deficit before hypothetical rescue. Ordinary base/bear shareholder IRRs are null.
evidence.locator: Embedded forward_model inputs, all five annual rows, financing sensitivities and rescue dilution
evidence.qualification: Forecast assumptions are explicitly not company guidance or bank commitments. Source anchors are audited opening accounts only.

evidence.claim: At ₹96.30, dated market cap ₹105.1596 cr and conservative debt/cash-adjusted EV ₹180.1327 cr imply reported P/E8.53× and EV/operating EBITDA 6.56×.
evidence.locator: Embedded valuation bridge; price19October with March2026 balance sheet
evidence.qualification: Date/perimeter mismatch and financing uncertainty prevent a supported base fair value.

valuation.qualification: Mixed dates: 19 October close with 31 March balance sheet and first-year consolidated earnings. No supported funding-adjusted base value; displayed multiples are descriptors, not evidence of cheapness.

qualifications: Audited 31 March 2026 balance sheet is carried unchanged to 19 October 2026. No intervening cash/debt assertion is made. The 6 October KBM equity outflow is separately deducted once in year 1 because no updated balance sheet is available.
Reported first-year consolidated sales are a scenario scale, not a verified run-rate or organic base; full-year/post-acquisition reconciliation is unresolved.
Forecast core ONWC = inventory + receivables - trade payables. All other net operating balances held constant, not released into cash.
Existing term principal beyond the disclosed next-year amount is a stress schedule, not verified facility amortization. Rolling bank and related debt renewal is conditional and unverified.
No undrawn facility is invented. All interest is cash paid in this model. Losses generate no current cash tax credit. No dividends.
All amounts INR crore except price and share count; crore/crore gives INR per share.
